newsitem.title: USA: Hills Stores to post charge from closures.
newsitem.headline: Hills Stores to post charge from closures.

text.p: Hills Stores Co said Monday it plans to close eight stores during this year's first quarter, resulting in a projected fourth quarter, after-tax charge of about $12.5 million, or about $1.10 per share.
The closures will reduce the chain's size from 165 stores to 157 stores. The stores to be closed are in North Carolina, Virginia and Ohio.

"Most of the affected stores were opened in 1994 and 1995 as part of a southern expansion strategy which was unsucessful and halted in mid-stream," President and Chief Executive Gregory Raven said in a statement.
"As a result, the penetration level required to successfully compete in these markets was never achieved."

The company said each of the stores to be closed was unprofitable, posting combined annual losses of more than $5 million. The pre-tax charge related to closures is about $21 million, the company said. The charge is to be posted in the fourth quarter ending February 1.
The stores are expected to close by late March or early April, Hills said.
A total of 440 full-time workers and 360 part-time workers will be affected by the shutdowns.
